10 Questions to Ask Before Hiring an Event Management Company

Your event is only as good as the team behind it. The right event management company turns your vision into a flawless experience; the wrong one turns it into a stressful, expensive lesson. Before you sign a contract, ask these ten questions — the answers will tell you everything you need to know.

1. What experience do you have with events like mine?

A wedding specialist and a conference specialist are not interchangeable. Ask for relevant examples and case studies that match your event type, size and audience.

2. Can I see your portfolio and references?

Photos tell one story; references tell another. Speak to past clients about reliability, problem-solving and how the team handled things when something went wrong.

3. Who will actually manage my event?

You might be sold by a senior pitch, then handed to a junior team. Confirm exactly who your point of contact and on-ground lead will be — and that they'll be there on the day.

4. How do you structure pricing?

Look for transparent, itemised costing — not a single vague number. Understand what's included, what's extra, and how change requests are billed. A trustworthy partner shares this openly.

5. How do you handle budgets and overruns?

Ask how they protect your budget and what happens if costs rise. The best companies build in a contingency and flag risks early rather than surprising you with a bigger bill.

6. What does your vendor network look like?

Strong vendor relationships mean better quality and rates. Ask whether they use trusted partners, can work with your preferred vendors, or both.

7. Can you manage the full scope end to end?

One accountable team beats juggling five agencies. Confirm whether they handle strategy, design, production, logistics and on-ground delivery — or only part of it.

8. How do you plan for things going wrong?

Events are live; something always shifts. Ask about their contingency planning, backups for critical AV, and how they've handled real on-day emergencies before.

9. How will we communicate during planning?

Clear, regular communication prevents most event disasters. Ask about their process — updates, timelines, approvals and who you contact when you need a fast answer.

10. How do you measure success?

A great partner cares about your outcome, not just the optics. Ask how they'll help you measure results against your goals — attendance, engagement, leads or feedback.

The right questions upfront save you from the wrong partner later. Don't be afraid to ask all ten.
